doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing lead trombone and Ginnie Powell
summary: Mandel says he followed Trummy Young and Tommy Pederson as lead trombonist in Raeburn's band on high chops, and mentions singer Ginnie Powell.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you play lead when you were on Raeburn’s band?
Yeah, I did. I did.
So by that time…
I sort of followed Trummy Young.
That’s quite an act to follow.
It sure is and Tommy Pederson before that. I couldn’t play like that, you know I really wasn’t that good, but for some reason I fitted.
And you had the high chops.
I had the high chops, yeah.
Well, so after…
I couldn’t play low worth a damn.
[laughs] So, after playing trombone for only about a year you were playing lead trombone in some of the…
Biggest, best bands in the country.
Yeah.
I didn’t know any better. I should never have done it.
[laughs]
But then I did it, what the hell.
And obviously pulled it off.
I pulled it off, yeah.
Oh, about Raeburn’s band, at that time what, Ginnie Powell was…
Yeah.
The singer right, Boyd’s wife.
She came into the band and she was a good singer, good singer and a nice girl.
